aspects.says: A text block removes escaped quotes and seams but has no interpolation: ${name} is plain text, and values go in through formatted, + or bind parameters.
basis: section:A Text Block Removes the Escaped Quotes and the Seams, Not the Backslashes or the Values

aspects.says: A text block still processes backslash escapes, so a regex or a path in it doubles its backslashes as before.
basis: section:A Text Block Removes the Escaped Quotes and the Seams, Not the Backslashes or the Values
section:Design Note: Why a Text Block Still Processes Escapes

aspects.says: A -- comment in a statement joined from literals without line breaks comments out everything after it, so a DELETE or UPDATE loses its WHERE and changes every row.
basis: section:A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It

aspects.says: Inside a traditional literal every quote and backslash meant for the text is written with a backslash in front, so text for another language that has escapes of its own (JSON, regex, a Windows path) carries two layers.
basis: section:Every Quote and Backslash Is Written Twice, and a Wrong Backslash Can Still Compile

aspects.says: A + expression made only of literals is folded into one string by javac, so splitting a literal across lines costs nothing at run time.
basis: section:A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It

aspects.says: \n is a single line feed on every platform, while %n, println and System.lineSeparator() write the line.separator the JVM started with, so a format with fixed line endings needs the escape it requires.
basis: section:`\n` Is Always a Line Feed; `%n`, `println` and `lineSeparator()` Follow the Platform

aspects.says: Text built with %n compared with an expected value written with \n matches on Linux and differs on Windows.
basis: section:`\n` Is Always a Line Feed; `%n`, `println` and `lineSeparator()` Follow the Platform

aspects.says: A value built from literals joined with + holds only what is between the quotes, so a missing line break or space at a seam joins two lines or two words, and a SQL -- comment then swallows the rest of the statement.
basis: section:A Value Split Across Lines Has a Seam at Every `+`, and a Missing `\n` or Space There Changes It

aspects.says: String templates were previews in Java 21 and 22 and were withdrawn.
basis: section:A Text Block Removes the Escaped Quotes and the Seams, Not the Backslashes or the Values
aspects.reason: a release-history fact about a withdrawn preview; nothing a reader writes or decides depends on it, and it is stated only to rule interpolation out

aspects.says: Only escapes javac doesn't know are errors; a single backslash before t, n, b, r, f or s compiles and silently puts a control character or a space into a path or a regex.
basis: section:Every Quote and Backslash Is Written Twice, and a Wrong Backslash Can Still Compile
